checks.observed: No roll-to-hit or dice mechanic in the input path. Every action resolves deterministically from an edge; M-K23 gives p100 = 1 frame over 200 inputs with 0 never consumed, which is incompatible with a probabilistic gate. Re-observed in my own --self-test run, not carried over from round 1.

No pause mid-fight. M-P12 disconnects the pad during play and the sim advances 301 frames with 0 modal surfaces — seam S14 upheld on the exact case the item predicts (a telescopic USB-C pad jogging loose). Noted with some irony: that same disconnect, taken during calibration rather than during play, is the biggest gap in this verdict.

No input-driven animation cancel. M-K6/M-K7 release held actions within 1 frame of blur and visibilitychange while recording displacement_after_commitment_m = 0.0000 — the committed state finishes and only then does the release take effect.

S33 applied rather than used as cover: M-K24 reports pipeline_drops 0 over 10 000 inputs beside aggregate_droppedInputs 9487, in separate counters, summed in neither direction. A press lost in transport is zero; a press refused by a combat window is the combat system working.

S35 reconciled correctly. There is a map and it is a menu screen; the action set stays closed at sixteen so no `map` action was invented. Measured on 844x390 handheld: world 11 controls, map ['__drawer'], journal ['__drawer'], inventory 11 (correctly not suppressed — you act in an inventory), world restored to 11. Eleven combat marks across a chart of the coast would have been an objective marker arrived at from the other side; they are not there. The drawer, which carries `menu`, stays, so a touch-only player can still close the screen.

Every refusal is in fiction and none is a control legend. Ctrl+W and F5 are refused with 'The bindings hold. That hand belongs to the window, not to you.' The calibration prompts are 'Swing.', 'Get out of the way.', 'Take it on the shield.', 'Stop and think.' — an instruction to the character, not to the hand. No control name appears on any of the eleven drawn marks.

The instruction budget is respected in the drawn frame, not only in the model: DS1's zero tutorial budget is met and DS2's sanctioned alternative is now actually shipped — 10 inscriptions across 5 states, 4 before the first meaningful choice, every DS4 verb covered, none addressing the player.

ar3.observed: One real crossing, unchanged from round 1 and not inflated: the input layer refuses presses the combat model rejects and keeps that refusal in a counter distinct from transport loss, so a Morrowind-side window refusing a Souls-side press is observable rather than conflated with a dropped input. Nothing this round widened it. Recorded as thin.

perturbInput() edits the document as the running game holds it and the change reaches the world on the next poll — every consumer reads the document rather than a copy taken at boot. Independently, the calibration permutation I taught an unrecognised pad changed which action a raw index produced in the running world, which is the same property observed from the defect side.

arbitration.notes: S32 respected: the raw 0.14 deadzone is owned here as a device property and nothing in this verdict claims anything about the response curve above it, which belongs to RI-CAM02.

biggest_gap.what: Round 2's build fix guards the COMPLETED calibration by pad id — `const perm = this.calibrationResult && this.calibrationResult.id === st.id ? ... : null` — and I re-derived it: calibrate a stranger through all six prompts, unplug, plug in a standard pad, and index 0 fires `interact` and index 5 fires `light`. Correct. But nothing guards the calibration IN PROGRESS. `this.calibration` is instance state with no pad id on it, `_beginCalibration()` is triggered from `_adoptPad()`, `_dropPad()` never clears it, and it never times out. `poll()` then runs `_calibrationPoll(st)` against whatever pad is currently active. Measured on dcf1d36 with my own driver: answer 2 of 6 prompts on an unrecognised pad, unplug it (n_pads 0) -> `calibrating: true`, prompt still 3/6; plug in a mapping:'standard' pad -> indices 0, 1, 2 and 3 ALL produce NOTHING, a completely dead pad; those four presses are consumed as the stranger's calibration answers and the prompt advances 3/6 -> 5/6; finishing the sequence writes result_id 'Xbox 360 Controller (XInput STANDARD GAMEPAD)' carrying the stranger's permutation, after which index 0 fires `roll`, index 4 `menu` and index 5 `lock_on`; after 600 further frames it is still calibrating.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: This is the same player-visible symptom the round's own commit message claims to have fixed — 'Calibrate one gamepad and the next one you plug in fires the wrong buttons' — reached by an ordinary route instead of an exotic one. The owner plugs a GameSir X2s in its DualSense-like HID mode, the game correctly starts the six-prompt calibration, and the USB-C connector jogs loose. That is not a hypothetical: it is the exact scenario M-P12 was written for and passes on. They re-seat it or reach for a normal pad, and the pad is dead with an in-fiction prompt on screen that never goes away. On a phone, index 0 is the only index there ever is. The round's one build fix and its one repaired instrument were pointed at the same route into the same defect and neither was asked what else could get there — M-P15 only ever calibrates and never disconnects.
biggest_gap.not_a_hard_fail_because: I checked rather than assumed whether this is HF10 / M-N5's 'unrecoverable loss of control'. It is not: with the calibration stuck I read the touch layout and drove it, all sixteen actions are still reachable and `light` still fires, so on a handheld the glass stays live. RI-JRN04 HF2 ('a scrambled map, or a refusal to run, on a mapping !== standard device') produces both consequences here and the non-standard device is the cause, but the device the scrambled map appears ON is the standard one, so the gate's literal subject is not met and I have not applied it. An arbiter reading HF2 by purpose rather than wording should cap RI-JRN04 at 2, and I would not argue.

remedy.action: game/src/input/gamepad.js, in _dropPad() after `this.pads.delete(idx)`: `if (st && this.calibration && !this.calibration.done) this.calibration = null;` — a calibration belongs to the pad it was begun on, exactly as the completed result now does. I applied this in the page and re-ran the identical sequence: `calibrating: false` after the unplug, and the standard pad's index 0 fires `interact` and index 5 fires `light`. Delete-the-fix reproduces the defect exactly, in both directions.
remedy.acceptance: A --self-test leg that begins a calibration, disconnects the pad mid-sequence, connects a mapping:'standard' pad and asserts index 0 fires `interact` — and that the leg goes red when the one line is removed. Plus M-P15 extended to run its sequence a second time with a disconnect at prompt 3, reporting the action the pad really fired when it is not `interact`, which is the property the repaired M-K18/M-P23 already have.

The stick is floating by design ('the stick originates wherever the thumb lands', which is the right engineering choice for a device whose size is unknown) and the eleven drawn marks are all in the right-hand thumb arc, so there is no drawn affordance for movement anywhere.

Recorded because §F's mechanism is that what the player can see, they can try, and this is the most likely thing a naive pass will find first. The naive pass has still not been run.

secondary_observations.what: The working tree does not boot. `node tools/harness/boot-check.mjs` exits 12 with 'TypeError: this._stepAmbience is not a function' — a sibling's uncommitted W1-22 edit put a call site in Engine._afterStep() before the method existed. This is the third time in this project that a call site has landed ahead of its method and the second time in two rounds that it has cost a measurement pass wall clock.

Reported because an orchestrator reading only per-piece verdicts will not otherwise see that the shared tree is red, and because the previous round's builder lost a complete self-test pass to exactly this ('Engine._boot: SoulsSystem is not defined').

secondary_observations.what: M-K22's repair is the right kind and is worth protecting. Round 1's substring matcher fired on sixteen ordinary Argonian names ('Waits-For-Salt the Shorter' -> 'rt'). The two token classes now have separate matchers, `-` is a word boundary, and the check reports `unmeasurable` if its own three-hit/three-miss lexicon control fails rather than grading with a broken lexicon. It enumerated 195 prompt strings in my run.
secondary_observations.note: A check that fires on nothing real trains its reader to ignore it, which is the mirror image of a check that cannot fire at all. Both halves are now handled.

arbitration_questions.question: Does RI-JRN04 HF2 fire on a scrambled map that appears on a mapping:'standard' device as a direct consequence of a mapping !== 'standard' device having been present?
arbitration_questions.why_it_matters: HF2 reads 'a scrambled map, or a refusal to run, on a mapping !== standard device'. The defect in §7 produces both listed consequences and the non-standard device is the cause, but the device that ends up scrambled is the standard one. Read literally the gate does not fire and RI-JRN04 scores 81; read by purpose it fires and RI-JRN04 caps at 2, which would take the piece to 2/10. I have taken the literal reading so as not to stretch a gate, exactly as round 1 declined to claim an HF5 it had not driven — but the difference between 6 and 2 should be a ruling and not a critic's discretion.
arbitration_questions.my_provisional_answer: Literal reading; not applied. Recorded so an arbiter can overrule cheaply.

corpus_extended.what: H10's legibility floor covers dialogue, journal and book, and nothing anywhere covers the HUD. On the item's own phone configuration the HUD's smallest run is 3.97 CSS px against a floor of 18, and it is the one surface a player looks at for the whole session.
corpus_extended.proposal: Add a fourth surface to H10, or a separate M-P2x, measuring the smallest run inside the declared hud.* rects at the same configuration and against the same floor. M-P20 already computes it — my probe reports it from the same data in the same pass — so this costs the instrument nothing.

self_audit.self_audit_note: ran_every_assigned_method is FALSE and this is the honest record: AR-1, AR-2, AR-3 and CONSUMPTION were all run first-hand, but the naive passes were not and must not be by me. On judged_output_not_source: in every case the measurement came first — the ablation before game/src/ui/touch-overlay.js was opened, the gamepad sequence in the browser before game/src/input/gamepad.js was read for the cause, M-P20 re-derived before mp20()'s implementation was read. The one exception is honest and stated: I read _dropPad() and _applyButtons() and FORMED the disconnect hypothesis from the code, then confirmed it in the running browser before writing it down, and applied and removed the fix in the page in both directions. On breaking what I measured: M-K20 was driven red through the shipped uiToast path; the overlay was ablated by severing _uiCtx and restored; the touch consumption legs carry two null controls (a still thumb and dead glass) that both produce nothing; the gamepad fix was applied and removed with the same sequence run either side. Two of my own probes produced results I discarded rather than published — an unstable null control and an undefined-coordinate press that read exactly like a coupling-zero — and both are in method_deviations because either would have been a false finding. Neither item carries blind_pair: yes, so no blind pack was owed.

notes: Round 1 scored 5/10 and its summary was 'the controls exist, work, are correctly laid out, and are drawn nowhere'. That is no longer true and the change is real: I photographed the controls, the ablation is clean in both directions with two stable null controls, every one of the eleven moves the world against two silent null controls, the rendered-text register is fed by the draw call across all three surfaces and goes red when I draw a forbidden string through the shipped toast, and all fourteen previously-absent check ids are function bodies with perturbation legs. The round also found and fixed a real build defect on its own, correctly, and proved it by delete-the-fix. It still fails, for one reason above all: the fix and the repaired instrument were both aimed at one route into a defect that has two, and the second route is a cable jogging loose.
